technical_and_design_decisions: Implement chaincode friendly names as a backward-compatible metadata field, while retaining the existing chaincode identifier as the canonical internal key.
Use the Fabric lifecycle system chaincode as the control point for chaincode deployment and upgrade policies, with policy validation performed before committing lifecycle changes.
Implement Solo as a single-process ordering service using a buffered input channel, one block-assembly loop, and an in-memory ledger supporting block history and client seek operations.
Treat the Solo in-memory ledger as a development and test feature rather than a production-durable ordering implementation.
Expose the state cache through a controlled peer-side API with concurrency protection, cache invalidation on committed state changes, and a defined behavior for cache misses.
Extract operator-facing commands into a standalone CLI package with minimal dependencies on peer internals, distributed as platform-specific binaries.
Publish the source repository through GitHub and organize documentation around chaincode development, application development, operations, lifecycle management, and upgrade procedures.
Use automated unit, integration, and end-to-end tests for lifecycle management, Solo ordering and delivery, state-cache behavior, CLI operations, and backward compatibility.
assumptions: The existing Hyperledger Fabric codebase, protobuf definitions, build system, peer services, and ordering-service interfaces are available and can be modified.
The specification describes one software increment, but all eight user stories are included in the estimate.
Existing cryptographic identity, membership, access-control, and policy primitives will be reused rather than redesigned.

The lifecycle system chaincode integrates with existing chaincode deployment mechanisms; the estimate covers the required integration and policy behavior, not a complete redesign of chaincode execution.
Solo supports a single orderer process and in-memory recovery only; persistent storage, crash recovery, high availability, and Byzantine fault tolerance are out of scope.
The state cache is local to a peer process and is intended to accelerate read/write-set construction; distributed cache coherence is out of scope.

The GitHub and documentation work includes repository publication or mirroring configuration, navigation, contribution guidance, and user-facing documentation, but not a complete redesign of the Hyperledger website.
The standalone CLI must support the principal existing peer and network-management operations needed by the stated user story, but does not need to expose every internal peer capability.
Testing includes representative supported platforms and mocked or local development networks; exhaustive compatibility testing across all operating systems is out of scope.
Effort includes implementation, code review preparation, automated tests, documentation, integration, and defect correction by one developer. Calendar duration and external waiting time are excluded.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing architecture and interfaces, map the eight user stories to affected components, define compatibility constraints, and produce implementation-level designs for lifecycle management, Solo ordering, state caching, CLI extraction, and documentation.

Add friendly-name data structures and APIs, update chaincode registration and lookup paths, preserve compatibility with existing identifiers, update command output and diagnostics, and add unit and integration tests.

Implement lifecycle system chaincode operations for installing or registering definitions, setting and retrieving deployment or endorsement policies, validating policy changes, handling authorization and errors, and integrating the lifecycle state with chaincode deployment and invocation paths.

Create unit, integration, negative, and compatibility tests covering policy validation, unauthorized changes, lifecycle upgrades, version transitions, and interaction with existing chaincode execution behavior.

Implement the single-process orderer, buffered submission channel, block batching loop, block numbering and metadata, startup and shutdown behavior, validation of incoming messages, and integration with the existing ordering-service interfaces.

activities.activity_name: Solo in-memory ledger and deliver/seek support
activities.activity_description: Implement the in-memory block ledger, client-specific history discovery, seek semantics, deliver-stream reconnection behavior, concurrency handling, memory limits or lifecycle behavior, and service error handling.

Add unit and end-to-end tests for concurrent submissions, block batching, ordering, delivery, disconnect and reconnect, seeking historical blocks, malformed requests, shutdown, and integration with a minimal application network.

Design and implement the peer-side state-cache API, cache population and lookup behavior, read/write-set construction integration, synchronization, invalidation after commits, cache-miss handling, and configurable cache limits.

Add cache unit and integration tests, stale-read and concurrent-access tests, commit-invalidation tests, failure-path tests, and representative performance measurements to verify that the cache improves read/write-set construction without changing ledger semantics.

Separate operator commands from peer internals, define stable command and configuration interfaces, remove unnecessary RocksDB and validating-peer dependencies, implement command wiring and user-friendly errors, and preserve compatibility with supported operations.

Create platform-specific build targets and installation artifacts, validate builds on the supported desktop and server platforms, add version and help output, provide installation instructions, and test CLI interaction with local Fabric components.

activities.activity_name: GitHub source availability and repository setup
activities.activity_description: Prepare the source repository for GitHub visibility, configure repository metadata and basic contribution guidance, verify that the relevant code and build instructions are accessible, and document the canonical source location.

Write documentation for chaincode and application development, lifecycle policy management, chaincode upgrade flows, Solo deployment and testing, state-cache usage, CLI installation and commands, and links or navigation to related Hyperledger documentation.

Build representative end-to-end scenarios combining lifecycle deployment, policies, chaincode naming, Solo ordering, state-cache operation, and standalone CLI administration; execute regression testing and correct integration defects.

activities.activity_name: Final review, release preparation, and handoff
activities.activity_description: Perform final code cleanup, API and configuration review, security and error-handling review, update examples and release notes, verify reproducible builds and documentation links, and prepare the increment for delivery.
